title: Free placement channels
description: Channels where a link can be published at no cost. Every record must be backed by something observed in a live page, never inferred from a sibling site or from documentation.

id.description: Stable slug. Never reuse an id for a different channel — dead records stay, with status: dead.

kind.description: guestbook-engine and publish-platform behave differently enough that they are not merged: an engine covers many host sites at once.

scope.description: engine means one codebase across many independent hosts. Engine records describe mechanics only; per-host settings (robots, anti-bot questions, moderation) must be probed per host and never generalised from one sample.

urlPattern.description: For channels where visiting a templated URL is the entire submission, e.g. https://example.com/{domain}. Use {domain} as the placeholder.

captcha.description: passive = clears itself in an ordinary browser with no user action. interactive = a real challenge; those channels are rejected, never solved.

anchorRendered.description: Whether a real <a href> is emitted. Some platforms publish your URL as a plain text node — those are worth nothing and must be recorded as false, not omitted.

relObserved.description: The exact rel strings read from the DOM. Empty array means dofollow was observed (no rel attribute). Omit the field entirely if never checked — never guess.

robotsObserved.description: The exact robots meta content of the page carrying the link, or null when the tag is absent (which means indexable). 'varies' is only acceptable when scope is engine.

indexable.description: true / false, or "per-host" for engine-scope records.

rateLimit.description: Observed limit and its scope, e.g. 'per address across the whole engine, ~8 posts per few hours'.

traps.description: Failure modes that produce plausible but wrong results. This is the highest-value field in the record — prefer adding one over adding a new channel.

status.description: rejected = technically works but disqualified on safety or value grounds; the reason belongs in rejectReason.

verifiedBy.description: GitHub handle of whoever last verified. Optional; omit rather than inventing.

notes.description: One-liner provenance for a field that isn't self-evident from evidence.what — e.g. where captcha's value came from, or that a mismatch found during a real submission was just corrected here. Omit rather than pad; do not restate what evidence.what already says.

method.description: anonymous-http alone is insufficient to claim a channel is dead or emits no anchor — many pages are client-rendered or answer 403 to scripts. It is sufficient to confirm what IS present.

what.description: What was actually observed, in one sentence.

publicUrl.description: A live page carrying a real placement, when one can be shared.
